chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-Khathʿamī narrated from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: "May I be your ransom, what do you say regarding al-Kanʿat?" He said, "There is no harm in eating it." I said, "It has no scales." He said, "Yes, it does, but it is a fish of bad disposition that rubs itself against everything, so when you look at the base of its ears, you will find that it has scales."

key_terms.أُذُنَيْهَا: Its ears; the place near which the scales are said to be found
key_terms.الْكَنْعَتِ: A specific type of fish being asked about in the ruling
key_terms.بِأَكْلِهِ: In eating it; consuming it as food
key_terms.سَيِّئَةُ الْخُلُقِ: Of bad disposition; described as rubbing against things
key_terms.قِشْرٌ: Scales, the physical feature relevant to the ruling on the fish
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no legal objection or harm; it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is al-Kanʿat fish halal to eat if its scales are not clearly visible?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the permissibility of eating a particular kind of fish, al-Kanʿat. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام explains that it is permissible because it does in fact possess scales, even if they are not immediately apparent. The report is significant for jurisprudence because it links the ruling to a physical characteristic relevant to halal status.
